Where I got to
I reconstructed the working tree from dump.txt with SHA-256 verification: 364 of 365 files verified byte-for-byte (LICENSE is metadata-only in the dump; export.sh is a parser false-positive from its own embedded header). Your terminal log confirms 1250 tests passing, which matches the Slice 54 prediction exactly — no drift this session.

I found the 500, and it is not where the plan expected
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Pages/Administration/ManageMenuItem.razor, line 272:

razor
                <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Save caption</button>
            </EditForm>          ← line 270

            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AltTextInput.AltText)" />   ← line 272, OUTSIDE
        }
ValidationMessage<T>.OnParametersSet() throws InvalidOperationException when there is no cascading EditContext. It is a sibling of the EditForm, not a child, so it gets none.

The whole block is inside @if (_picture is not null). That explains the symptom precisely:

You POST the upload. During that render _picture is still null (OnInitializedAsync runs before the submit event dispatches), so the block never renders — the POST succeeds, the row is written, the redirect is issued.
The browser follows the redirect to /administration/menu/{id}?done=picture-attached. Now _picture is not null, the block renders, ValidationMessage throws → 500.
The nastier consequence: that page is 500 on every GET from then on, so you cannot even reach Remove picture to undo it. Nothing in the suite could see it — MenuItemImageSurfaceContractTests reads the markup as text, and no §16.3 scenario has ever uploaded a picture.

I also ruled out the candidates I'd have otherwise guessed at: the media-type vocabularies in 0006 and ImageFormat agree; the over-cap path is covered against real PostgreSQL by BytesOverTheSchemasCapAreRefusedWithNothingWritten; Blazor's RazorComponentEndpointInvoker does read the multipart form asynchronously before dispatch, so Request.Form.Files is sound; and enhanced-nav form handling passes FormData through unchanged for multipart/form-data.

What I was building toward, and what I need from you
I had the slice scoped as M6 Slice 55, and I'd sketched it against the gates it has to satisfy:

F-106 — the fix, plus a new computed-subject gate asserting every ValidationMessage/ValidationSummary in the component tree sits inside an EditForm in the same file. It is proven sensitive by the tree as it stands right now, which is the strongest form of that proof this project asks for.
Browser downscaling (the plan's named next slice) — a classic script in wwwroot/js/, createImageBitmap → <canvas> → toBlob, swapped into the file input via DataTransfer so the existing multipart transport is untouched. No blob: or object URLs, so img-src and script-src 'self' stay exactly as they are. The byte budget read live from pg_constraint rather than restated, so 512 KiB still lives only in 0006.
§16.3 scenario 18 — the picture round trip, which is what would have caught F-106.
I ran out of tool budget while reading the §16.4 counted-class paragraphs I need to keep in step (MinimumCountedClasses = 29, and MenuItemImageSurfaceContractTests is pinned at ten assertions there).

Say go and I'll author it and deliver the structured .tar.gz — full files, repo-relative paths, explicit delete list, git add lines for the new files, and the documentation updated atomically. One question worth ruling on before I start, since it changes the shape:

Do you want scenario 18 in this slice, or held for the next one? Including it is the honest proof the 500 is gone, but it is the largest new surface and the one I cannot exercise from here. Fix + gate + downscaling alone is the lower-risk delivery.

The slice delivery note

Clear the previous slice's delivery note
I hit the tool limit one call short of writing the new _CHANGES.md and packaging the archive. Everything else is done and verified in my container — but I can't hand you the tarball this turn. Here is exactly where things stand so you can pick it up in one message.

The 500 — root cause confirmed
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Pages/Administration/ManageMenuItem.razor had <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AltTextInput.AltText)" /> one line below </EditForm>, inside @if (_picture is not null). A sibling of an EditForm gets no cascading EditContext, and ValidationMessage.OnParametersSet throws without one.

The attaching POST renders while _picture is still null → block doesn't render → upload succeeds, commits, redirects.
The redirected GET is the first render where a picture exists → throws → 500.
Every later view of that item answered 500, including the one with the Remove button — not reversible from any surface.
Your report named the wrong request, which is why it was hard to find. Fixed by moving the tag inside the form.

What I completed and mechanically checked
F-106 fix in ManageMenuItem.razor.
EditContextConsumerContractTests (new, 2 facts). Verified: 51 components, 83 consumers, 0 findings on the repaired tree; 1 finding at line 216 against the file as it shipped — sensitivity proven against the real defect.
Stage 4e downscaler: new wwwroot/js/menu-picture.js, loaded from App.razor; MenuItemImageUpload gains the attribute names, status element id and LongestEdgePixels; IMenuItemImageDirectory.ReadDeclaredByteCapAsync reads the cap from pg_get_constraintdef. No CSP change needed — createImageBitmap + canvas.toBlob never produce a URL.
F-107 gate: MenuItemImageSurfaceContractTests 10 → 12 facts. Verified: bound parses out of 0006 as 524288, 178 files under src/ scanned, zero restatements (I stripped the digits from my own new doc comment to keep that true).
PictureFixtures (new) — generates a real PNG at any size. Verified by re-implementing its exact arithmetic and decoding: 12px → 512 bytes, 640px → 1,229,598 bytes (2.34× cap), JPEG q82 → ~16 KB.
